Research Question and Objectives
Research Question: Where are forest-fire events concentrated within Ketapang Regency, and how does their spatial distribution and interaction change across the observed 2026 period (particularly as the dry season progresses)?

title: Geospatial Analytics for Public Safety
text:
Data and Study Design
Study area: Ketapang Regency, West Kalimantan, Indonesia.
Core datasets:

Forest-fire event data: NASA FIRMS, VIIRS S-NPP (SV-C2) and VIIRS NOAA-20 (J1V-C2), bounding box 109.8, -3.2, 111.3, 0.0, observation period 1 Jan 2026 – 12 Sept 2026, Shapefile format.
Administrative boundary data: indonesia-geospasial.com, “Batas Administrasi Kabupaten/Kota Tahun 2019” (Indonesia regency boundaries), filtered to Ketapang Regency.

First-Order Spatial Point Pattern Analysis

Preparing the Point Pattern Object

# Convert Ketapang boundary to an owin (observation window) for spatstat
ketapang_owin <- as.owin(ketapang_boundary)

# Extract coordinates from the cleaned fire points
fire_coords <- st_coordinates(fire_ketapang_clean)

# Create the ppp (planar point pattern) object
fire_ppp <- ppp(x = fire_coords[,1], 
                 y = fire_coords[,2], 
                 window = ketapang_owin)

# Targeted checks instead of full summary()
n_dupes_ppp <- sum(duplicated(fire_ppp))
n_points_final <- fire_ppp$n
n_points_original <- nrow(fire_coords)

Temporal Variation in Fire Intensity (Phase-Based)

# Define fire phase based on documented 2026 Kalimantan wildfire escalation timeline
fire_ketapang_clean <- fire_ketapang_clean %>% 
  mutate(phase = case_when(
    ACQ_DATE < as.Date("2026-07-01") ~ "Pre-escalation (Jan-Jun)",
    ACQ_DATE < as.Date("2026-08-01") ~ "Onset (Jul)",
    TRUE ~ "Crisis (Aug-Sep)"
  ),
  phase = factor(phase, levels = c("Pre-escalation (Jan-Jun)", "Onset (Jul)", "Crisis (Aug-Sep)")))

table(fire_ketapang_clean$phase)

# Split ppp object by phase (factor levels set in phase-kde-prep control order)
fire_ppp_phase <- fire_ppp
marks(fire_ppp_phase) <- fire_ketapang_clean$phase

fire_split_phase <- split(fire_ppp_phase)

# KDE per phase, same bandwidth (bw_diggle) for comparability across panels
kde_phase <- lapply(fire_split_phase, function(p) density(p, sigma = bw_diggle, edge = TRUE))

par(mfrow = c(1,3), mar = c(1,1,2,1))
for (ph in names(kde_phase)) {
  plot(kde_phase[[ph]], main = ph)
  plot(ketapang_boundary$geometry, add = TRUE, border = "white")
}

Hot Spots and Cold Spots Analysis (HCSA)

Deriving Distance Weight Matrix

ct <- critical_threshold(st_geometry(hunan))
ct

hunan_fdw <- hunan %>% 
  mutate(nb = include_self(
    st_dist_band(

  mutate(nb = include_self(
    st_knn(
      st_geometry(geometry),
      k = 6)),

      nb, style = "W"),
    .before = 1)



Computing Local Gi*

set.seed(1234)
HCSA_fdw <- hunan_fdw %>%
  mutate(
    gistar = local_gstar_perm(
      GDPPC, nb, wt, nsim = 99),
    .before = 1) %>%
  unnest(gistar)



Preparing and Visualising HCSA Map

Mapping Gi* with Fixed Distance Weights

tm_shape(HCSA_fdw) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "gi_star",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
                style = "pretty",
                n = 6,

                position = tm_pos_out())) + 
  tm_borders(fill_alpha = 0.5) +

Mapping Local Gi* p-values

  tm_polygons(fill = "p_sim", 
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
                breaks = c(-Inf, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, Inf),

      position = tm_pos_out())) +

Mapping Both Gi* Values and p-values

  tm_polygons(fill = "gi_star",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
                style = "pretty",
                n = 5,
                values = "-brewer.rd_bu"),

                title = "local Gi*",
                position = tm_pos_in("left", "bottom"))) + 
  tm_borders(fill_alpha = 0.5) +
  tm_title("Local Gi* of GDPPC")


p_values_map <- tm_shape(HCSA_fdw) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "p_sim",

      position = tm_pos_in("left", "bottom")
    )) + 
  tm_borders(fill_alpha = 0.5) +
  tm_title("p-values of local Gi* of GDPPC (fixed distance)")


tmap_arrange(Gi_star_map, p_values_map, asp = 1, ncol = 2)










Plotting and Visualising HCSA Map

HCSA_fdw <- HCSA_fdw %>%
  mutate(HCSA_cluster = case_when(
    p_sim > 0.05 ~ "Insignificant",
    p_sim <= 0.05 & cluster == "High" ~ "Hot spot",
    p_sim <= 0.05 & cluster == "Low"  ~ "Cold spot",
    TRUE ~ "Other"),
    HCSA_cluster = factor(
      HCSA_cluster,
      levels = c("Insignificant", "Hot spot", "Cold spot")
    ),
    .before = 1
  )


HCSA_map <- tm_shape(HCSA_fdw) + 
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "HCSA_cluster",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(
      values = c(
        "grey80",
        "red",
        "blue"
      )
    ),
    fill.legend = tm_legend(
      title = "HSCA Cluster",
      position = tm_pos_in("left", "bottom"))
  ) +
  tm_borders() +
  tm_title("HCSA Clusters (p < 0.05)")
HCSA_map









tmap_arrange(Gi_star_map, HCSA_map, asp = 1, ncol = 2)








The Gi* statistic works differently from local Moran’s I, instead of looking for outliers vs clusters, it’s specifically hunting for hot spots (high values surrounded by other high values) and cold spots (low surrounded by low). This is why we needed distance-based neighbours instead of the contiguity-based ones from before, since Gi* is fundamentally about how much a location’s neighbourhood total compares to the overall average.

set.seed(1234)
lisa_nsim499 <- wm_q %>% 
  mutate(local_moran = local_moran(

  mutate(HCSA_cluster_adw = case_when(
    p_sim > 0.05 ~ "Insignificant",
    p_sim <= 0.05 & cluster == "High" ~ "Hot spot",
    p_sim <= 0.05 & cluster == "Low"  ~ "Cold spot",
    TRUE ~ "Other"),
    HCSA_cluster_adw = factor(
      HCSA_cluster_adw,
      levels = c("Insignificant", "Hot spot", "Cold spot")
    )
  )

HCSA_map_adw <- tm_shape(HCSA_adw) + 
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "HCSA_cluster_adw",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(
      values = c("grey80", "red", "blue")
    ),
    fill.legend = tm_legend(
      title = "HSCA Cluster (adaptive)",
      position = tm_pos_in("left", "bottom"))
  ) +
  tm_borders() +
  tm_title("HCSA Clusters, Adaptive Weights (p < 0.05)")

tmap_arrange(HCSA_map, HCSA_map_adw, asp = 1, ncol = 2)








Worth comparing whether the hot spot/cold spot pattern actually changes depending on whether we use fixed distance neighbours or k=6 adaptive neighbours, since urban vs rural counties could get very different neighbourhood sizes under the fixed approach.

section: Spatio-temporal Point Patterns Analysis: stpp Methods
text:
Spatio-temporal Point Patterns Analysis: stpp Methods

pacman::p_load(stpp)

Switching over to the stpp package here, which gives us a different set of tools for space-time analysis, specifically the space-time K-function, which extends what we did with the regular K-function in the last exercise into the time dimension too.

coords <- st_coordinates(fire_sf)

fire_df <- data.frame(
  x = coords[, 1],  
  y = coords[, 2],
  t = fire_sf$DayofYear)

fire_stpp <- as.3dpoints(fire_df)
class(fire_stpp)

[1] "stpp"



plot(fire_stpp)








This just visualizes the raw fire points in 3D, x, y, and time together, before we run any actual statistics on them.

set.seed(1234)
kbb_stik <- STIKhat(fire_stpp)


plotK(kbb_stik)

The space-time K-function tells us whether fires cluster together in both space and time simultaneously, not just one or the other. If the contour plot shows high values at small spatial and temporal distances, that means fires that happen close together in space also tend to happen close together in time, which would make sense for something like slash-and-burn agriculture practices that spread across neighboring areas within short windows.

summary(kde_month_adaptive)

set.seed(1234)

  as.ppp()

plot(G_fire)








Ran a plain spatial G-function here (ignoring time completely) just to compare against the space-time K-function result above. If this alone shows clustering but doesn’t tell us anything about timing, it makes the case for why the spatio-temporal approach actually adds value instead of just being spatial analysis with extra steps.

fire_sf <- fire_sf %>%
  mutate(weekday = wday(acq_date, label = TRUE),

Just curious whether fire occurrence has any weekday pattern, humans starting fires (intentionally or by accident) might show a weekly rhythm, whereas naturally occurring fires probably wouldn’t care what day it is. Not expecting a huge effect here, but worth checking.
